statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is 3 and far below the block threshold because CME equity-index futures have been halted since Friday 21:00Z, leaving no Nasdaq-100 price path to score; the last observed path, Friday's new 31,017.53 intraday record fully retraced into a 30,807.93 close in the lower quarter of the 30,737.07-31,017.53 range with VIX down 6.59% to 15.31, is orderly two-way discovery rather than the extension pattern Tail measures. Stress is 70 in the high band because a record U.S. diesel squeeze, the G7's 100-million-barrel emergency release, an unconfirmed Houthi strike on a Riyadh Aramco facility and a 10-year that reversed higher to 5.2939% on a 29,000 payroll print accumulate with no venue able to price them. Confidence is 84: Friday's index, volatility, curve and crude levels are independently verified and the payroll data is taken from the primary release, with the absence of a live price path the one unavoidable gap.
recommendation: Tail remains in the low band for all 24 scored hours, so the deterministic mapping stays at EA_ON and green throughout. Every hour of this window falls inside the CME equity-index weekend halt, and the restart at 22:00Z on 4 October lies exactly at the end of the final scored hour, so restart gap risk is described rather than scored here. The Gulf cash session from roughly 07:00Z to 12:00Z on 4 October is the one differentiating interval and the only live venue with direct exposure to the claimed Riyadh refinery strike; under the inherited delayed-evidence rule it can inform Stress and Confidence but cannot establish current Nasdaq-100 structure or move the mapped action. Stress drifts from 70 to a peak of 79 and stays inside the high band, which on this contract does not by itself change the mapped state. No evidence-based danger window falls inside this horizon, so none is published.
headline: Weekend halt holds Tail at 3 with no Nasdaq-100 price path to score, while a record diesel squeeze, the G7's 100-million-barrel release and an unconfirmed Riyadh refinery strike keep Stress at 70
body:
Friday 2 October remains the last traded session and its levels are independently re-verified for this publication. The Nasdaq-100 closed at a record 30,807.93, up 306.37 points or 1.00% from a 30,501.56 previous close, inside a 30,737.07-31,017.53 session range whose high is also the 52-week high. The detail that matters most for this framework is that the new intraday record at 31,017.53 was fully retraced and the index finished in the lower quarter of its own daily range. That is orderly two-way price discovery, not the shallow-pullback extension or failed-retracement pattern that defines Tail, so Tail holds at 3. VIX closed at 15.31, down 6.59% from 16.39 and at the bottom of a 15.30-16.24 range, confirming volatility decay into the halt.

The session's driver was the September employment report, taken here from the primary release: nonfarm payrolls rose 29,000 against a 90,000 consensus, the unemployment rate was 4.2%, and average hourly earnings edged up 0.1% to $37.81 for a 3.0% annual rate. Equities read that as cementing a Fed hold at the 28 October meeting, but the curve did not follow: the 10-year traded as low as 5.17% immediately after the data before reversing to 5.2939%, about 6 basis points higher on the day, and the 2-year ended at 4.8414%, about 5 basis points higher. The Federal Reserve H.15 release for 1 October shows the 2-year at 4.78% and the 10-year at 5.24%, so Friday's move extended an already elevated curve. A record equity close against rising long yields on weak labour data is a legitimate Stress and Confidence input; on this contract it is not a Tail input.

The energy complex is the dominant Stress driver. The G7 and its partners agreed to release 100 million barrels of oil and refined products over four months, with a frontloaded substantial diesel release inside the first 20 days, after the U.S. national average diesel price reached a record $6.52 per gallon on 22 September and stood at $6.37 on Friday. The release is a direct response to a supply crunch with three identified sources: the U.S.-Israel war on Iran disrupting Gulf exports, Ukrainian strikes halting Russian refinery output, and China ceasing diesel exports. Brent briefly fell below $100 on the announcement before recovering to about $102.25, and WTI reached a one-month low near $88 before trimming losses to roughly $91. The U.S. administration has separately ruled out a diesel export ban, which removes one discontinuous policy path from the week ahead. Cited expert views hold that the release will press prices lower only briefly because underlying supply remains below normal.

Against that offset sits the escalation thread. A large plume of smoke and fire was reported near an Aramco facility in Riyadh on Saturday, and the Houthis later said they had targeted it with ballistic missiles and drones in retaliation for Saudi strikes on Sanaa and other Yemeni provinces. Saudi authorities have not confirmed an attack and Aramco has not commented; damage, casualties and any throughput effect remain unconfirmed. Elsewhere the Gaza ceasefire reached under the 20-point plan continues to hold with its later phases stalled rather than breaking, which is a persistent uncertainty rather than new escalation with market transmission. None of this is scoreable as a Nasdaq-100 price path while every relevant venue is closed, and on this contract event importance and geopolitical discontinuity raise Stress and shape Confidence until observed market structure supports Tail.

The week ahead is moderate on U.S. macro: ISM Services on Monday, the trade balance and a 3-year auction on Tuesday, FOMC minutes on Wednesday, jobless claims on Thursday and preliminary Michigan sentiment on Friday, with the next rate decision not until 28 October. The OPEC+ participating countries also meet online on Sunday to review November targets, which are widely expected to be left unchanged; because the exact hour is not reliably published it is carried as a driver checkpoint rather than as a dated calendar event. The shared Finviz context was not usable for this run: it was collected on 29 September, roughly four days old against the 90-minute freshness bound, and is marked partial, so the assessment rests entirely on independent research and the evidence failed open as the contract requires.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding clock-hours carry published Claude assessments. The window opens in the first hour after Friday's close with Tail 12 and Stress 72 under a mixed mode, then decays as the halt takes hold: Tail falls from 12 to 3 by 12:00Z and the mode settles to normal from 00:00Z onward. Stress troughs at 52 around 14:00Z on Saturday and then climbs steadily back to 69 by 21:00Z as the energy and Gulf escalation threads reopened and finally produced a claimed strike on a Riyadh refinery. Confidence held in a narrow 82 to 88 range throughout, consistent with verified session levels and no live price path.
outlookSummary: Every hour of this forecast window falls inside the CME equity-index weekend halt, so no Nasdaq-100 price path can form. Tail is held at 3 for the first seventeen hours and rises only to 6 in the final hours as the restart approaches, mapping to EA_ON and green throughout. Stress drifts from 70 to a peak of 79 and remains in the high band, because a record diesel squeeze, the G7's 100-million-barrel release, an unconfirmed Riyadh refinery strike and a 10-year that reversed higher to 5.2939% accumulate with no venue able to price them. Confidence eases from 84 to 81 overnight as Friday's levels age, lifts to 83 during the Gulf cash session when the only live venue with direct exposure can be observed, then settles at 79. The mode shifts from normal to mixed for the final eight hours, which is the honest label for a two-sided unpriced stack rather than an assertion of structure. The restart at 22:00Z on 4 October sits exactly at the end of the final scored hour and falls to later publications to score.
